_comment: A6 / red-team item 6: the declared, reviewed exceptions battery_verdict.py measures every real check_all.sh run against. Every entry names its class, a reason, the date recorded, a review_by date and a removal_condition. An exception PAST its review_by turns blocking (a failure cemetery is not allowed), and one that starts PASSING shows up as 'recovered', so a stale entry rots visibly rather than normalizing a permanent known failure. TEST GRANULARITY, 2026-09-03: an entry for a check whose FAIL output names its failing tests declares them under failing_tests, one reason and removal condition per test name, because an exception keyed on the whole check shelters every future failure in it too. The verdict diffs the log's failing names against the declared set, and its own schema check (battery_verdict.py --check-expectations) refuses an entry that declares only a count or only a suite.

negative-space-audit.reason: R27.2's generated negative-space contract audit reports NO-DATA (exit 2) by design for every cell nobody has answered yet; these are the honest open findings the mechanism exists to surface, not a broken check.
negative-space-audit.removal_condition: the open negative-space cells are answered or reviewed-exempt so the audit exits 0; then delete this entry
negative-space-audit.last_reverified: 2026-09-05: re-ran python3 scripts/negative_space_audit.py, still exit 2, same open-cells-by-design shape (no new class of failure).

wire-dual-principal.reason: VAULT-HARDENING-SCOPE-2026-08-31.md V3b: bm_vault_serve.py's served POST /recall reads no agent-shaped field (confirmed both statically, from its own source, and behaviorally, by sending every plausible spelling and observing no change in what is served); the CLI's VB3-04 dual-principal intersection guarantee (bm_vault_policy.decide_dual) is therefore unreachable at the buyer-facing HTTP boundary. scripts/test_wire_dual_principal.py records this as FAIL-BY-DESIGN, a defect record naming the gap, never new capability built to close it.
wire-dual-principal.removal_condition: the served /recall endpoint gains a second principal field (for example agent_identity) and applies decide_dual's intersection semantics at the wire, proven by scripts/test_wire_dual_principal.py exiting 0; then delete this entry
wire-dual-principal.failing_tests: none: the battery runs scripts/test_wire_dual_principal.py's main() probe, which prints one CAN or CANNOT verdict and exits 1 by design (FAIL-BY-DESIGN); its unittest class runs only under --unittest, so the check's output names no failing tests
wire-dual-principal.last_reverified: 2026-09-05: re-ran python3 scripts/test_wire_dual_principal.py, still exit 1, same FAIL-BY-DESIGN verdict (do_POST reads only identity, limit, query, tenant; no candidate agent field changed behavior).

evad-score.reason: the codex series of 2026-09-04 measured t1 FAIL after a Claude-reviewer PASS on 2026-09-01; the regression is real and carried by rows E79 to E81. AMENDED 2026-09-05 (BAT-103), because the entry named only the regression while the score line it shelters reads '1/3 (33%), 4 trial(s) NO-DATA': four of the seven gauntlet trials were never run, and the run record says why in its own words. t5 'codex workspace out of credits after 418 s, two of four steps done, no report', t6 'codex workspace out of credits after 315 s, no report', t7 'codex workspace out of credits at start', and t3 'the sandbox refused the tamper cleanup (rm style commands not permitted) so the one-byte tamper was not completed'. None of the four is a moved document or a broken script: the trials are driven by an external, credit metered agent workspace and a sandbox that refuses part of one trial's own teardown, so no session can re-measure them from this tree, and a score is never asserted by hand. They are recorded here so a reader of this entry cannot mistake 1/3 for a measured three trial series.
evad-score.removal_condition: a re-measured series records t1 PASS or the rows close and the next series holds; the four NO-DATA trials need a credited external workspace (t5, t6, t7) and a sandbox that permits t3's own tamper cleanup, and each one that runs is recorded through scripts/evad_score.py --record, never written in by hand
evad-score.failing_tests: none: the check runs scripts/evad_score.py, which is not a unittest suite; its FAIL output names gauntlet trial ids (t1..t7) rather than test names, and exits 1 by design whenever a trial regresses PASS to FAIL against the previous stored run
evad-score.last_reverified: 2026-09-05: re-ran python3 scripts/evad_score.py, still 1/3 (33%), t1 FAIL (REGRESSED), same shape as the declared reason; four of seven trials also read NO-DATA this run (codex workspace out of credits), which is separate from and does not change the declared t1 regression.

release-note-perturb.reason: PR 260 (row E116) put the real perturbation behind BROTHER_LONG_CHECKS because the run takes about 90 minutes on this tree, so an ordinary battery prints NO-DATA for it by design and says so in its own output line: 'long check (about 90 min) not run: set BROTHER_LONG_CHECKS=1'. The check itself is not broken and its self test (release-note-perturb-self) runs in every battery and reads PASS; what is undeclared here is only the deliberate skip. A real FAIL from scripts/release_note_perturb.py is not covered by this entry and still blocks.
release-note-perturb.removal_condition: the battery sets BROTHER_LONG_CHECKS=1 on release cuts and the check reads PASS there
release-note-perturb.failing_tests: none: the check is one script, not a unittest suite, and it is not run at all in the default battery, so its NO-DATA line names no test
